executive_summary.headline: Scientists are handing the experiment loop to agents, and a national lab shows what that looks like.
executive_summary.body: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory shows agents that interpret results mid-run, rewrite the protocol and code a liquid-handling robot for critical-materials recovery. Two Minute Papers adds an MIT CSAIL result where GPT-6 Astra edited 0.016% of a small model's weights and lifted its MATH-500 score from 7.9% to 48.1%.

executive_summary.headline: Building your own software is now the default move for solo creators.
executive_summary.body: Matthew Berman built a PDF reader and an outlier tracker himself, Riley Brown turned an old iPhone into a focus monitor that costs about nine cents for eight hours, and Matt Wolfe shows Claude editing his videos with skills learned from his best-performing ones.

executive_summary.headline: Open-weight models keep landing in bulk, from a 3T-parameter Kimi to a 1 GB on-device model.
executive_summary.body: Berman's roundup covers Kimi K3.1 Pro, NorthCUA computer-use models at up to 88 on OSWorld Verified and Liquid AI's LFM3 1.7B, while Sam Witteveen runs Ricursive's Apache-licensed Ripple 65B locally. Benchmark figures are the model makers' own.

top_picks.title: PNNL's Autonomous Lab That Designs Its Own Experiments
top_picks.summary: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory shows an autonomous lab where AI agents read results mid-experiment and change the protocol, instead of running a fixed script. The test case is recovering critical materials from complex chemical mixtures: the agents run a techno-economic analysis, form an extraction hypothesis and write the code that drives a liquid-handling robot. A researcher says interns used to spend 4 to 5 hours on sample prep. The 5-minute video is published by the lab itself.
top_picks.author: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory

secondary_urls.label: Nature: AutoDNA, an AI-native autonomous lab (Nov 4 2026)
Nature: agents that design a robot lab (Nov 6 2026)

key_takeaways: The lab separates automation (a preset workflow) from autonomy (agents that interpret results and adapt the protocol while the experiment runs).
The agents handle the whole loop for critical-materials recovery: economics, hypothesis, and robot code for the liquid handler.
The stated long-term goal is a self-learning lab system, with sample preparation as the first task handed to agents.
suggested_actions: Show this 5-minute video to your chemistry or materials scientists and ask which of their bench steps follows a fixed protocol that an agent could adapt.
Ask each R&D group for its slowest sample-prep or data-handling step and map it to the hypothesis, code and robot-run loop shown here.

top_picks.title: They did it...
top_picks.summary: Matthew Berman argues that building your own software is now cheaper than finding and paying for it. He shows Folio, an open-source PDF reader, and an Outlier Tracker built in about 30 minutes, says an Excel clone cost about $10 in tokens, and points to Artcraft, an open-source suite aimed at Adobe's apps. The video includes an NVIDIA RTX Spark sponsor segment (6:09 to 7:19).
top_picks.author: Matthew Berman

secondary_urls.label: TechRepublic: developer uses Claude to build 7 free Adobe alternatives (Artcraft)

key_takeaways: Berman built two small tools himself (a PDF reader and an outlier tracker), the second in roughly 30 minutes.
His cost claim for an Excel clone is about $10 in tokens; treat it as his estimate, not a benchmark.
Artcraft is the larger example: an open-source suite that recreates several Adobe-style apps.
suggested_actions: Pick one paid utility you use weekly and ask a coding agent for a first version this weekend.
Browse Artcraft and note which of its apps your creative team could replace or customize.

top_picks.title: 31 Life-Changing Ways to Use Claude in 2027
top_picks.summary: Nick Saraev lists 31 ways people use Claude, from a router that got 8x faster to a house walkthrough in 3D. The science stories stand out: about 30 Claude agents researched one person's cancer with a Dana-Farber lab reviewing the plan, about 1,500 scripts searched seven years of NASA telescope data and surfaced a planet candidate, and roughly 1,000 agents searched DNA data for a CRISPR-like enzyme. These are the video's anecdotes and are not independently verified. He also promotes his Maker School community.
top_picks.author: Nick Saraev
key_takeaways: Agents at scale are the common thread: dozens to a thousand agents working one question in parallel.
Three science examples (cancer research, telescope archives, enzyme discovery) show scientists using agents as a search layer over data they already hold.
Everyday examples include mapping about 150,000 Steam games to find gaps in the market.
suggested_actions: Pick the two examples closest to your business and run them as one-hour experiments.
Ask a scientist on your team which archive of old data an agent swarm could search.
Treat each anecdote as a lead and look for the underlying source before reusing a number.

top_picks.title: How I Get Claude To Edit My Videos (Step-By-Step)
top_picks.summary: Matt Wolfe walks through a Claude-based video editing setup using Opus 5.5, FFmpeg, Hyperframes, Blender and ElevenLabs. He builds reusable editing skills from his top-performing videos and refines them with feedback. His verdict is that the setup suits short-form talking-head content better than long-form. vidIQ sponsors the video.
top_picks.author: Matt Wolfe
key_takeaways: Editing skills are derived from the creator's own best-performing videos, then tuned with feedback.
The toolchain is open: FFmpeg, Hyperframes and Blender handle the edit, ElevenLabs the voice.
Wolfe says it works best for short-form talking-head content.
suggested_actions: Collect your three best-performing videos and have Claude write an editing style guide from them.
Test the workflow on one short clip before trying long-form.

top_picks.title: I Built My Most Useful App Ever (Full Guide)
top_picks.summary: Riley Brown turns an old iPhone into a focus monitor with Codex and an OpenAI vision call. The phone sends a screenshot every 30 seconds, the API labels it on-task, off-task or uncertain, and a nudge fires only after at least two minutes of confident off-task checks. He says 100 checks cost one cent and eight hours cost about nine cents. OpenAI sponsors the video.
top_picks.author: Riley Brown
key_takeaways: The whole app is a screenshot loop plus a three-way label, so it stays cheap: about nine cents for eight hours by his numbers.
A two-minute confidence window keeps the nudges from firing on every glance away.
Codex wrote the app on top of an open-source companion app, and an old phone is the hardware.
suggested_actions: Copy the three-label pattern (on-task, off-task, uncertain) for any camera or screen check you want to automate.
Dig out a spare phone and use it as a single-purpose AI device.

top_picks.title: OpenAI's Astra Just Opened The Black Box Of AI
top_picks.summary: Two Minute Papers covers a research post dated Nov 2; the authors say the work is not yet formally published. It uses GPT-6 Astra with code to inspect and edit weights; in a Qwen3.5-0.8B experiment, a 131,072-weight change (0.016%) raised MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1%. The authors also report no meaningful gain on Gemma 3 270M. This is a narrow proof of concept, not evidence that frontier LLMs natively understand weights. Lambda sponsors the video.
top_picks.author: Two Minute Papers

secondary_urls.label: Two Minute Papers video: OpenAI's Astra Just Opened The Black Box Of AI (Nov 7 2026)

key_takeaways: On Qwen3.5-0.8B, a 131,072-weight edit cut answers that hit the token limit from 93.0% to 33.1%, which explains most of the MATH-500 gain.
Written from scratch with no training, Astra's Breakout network scored 517.4 against 25.3 for PPO trained on 500 million steps.
Astra could not improve Gemma 3 270M, so the method does not yet work on every model.
suggested_actions: Read the MIT blog post and note which tasks a model could fix by editing a few weights instead of retraining.
Ask your research team whether a loop-failure fix of this kind applies to any small model you run.

sections.title: Tool and Model Updates
sections.description: Open-weight models, creative tools and simulation platforms released or covered this week.

items.title: Kimi K3.1 weights OUT, open source computer use, SOTA image model, science model, Pika H3: AI NEWS
items.summary: Berman's open-model roundup covers Kimi K3.1 Pro (3 trillion parameters, which he estimates needs at least 1.2 TB of VRAM) and NorthCUA computer-use models scoring 78.9, 85 and 88 on OSWorld Verified for Nano, Mini and Pro. Pruna's P-H3 Image makes a 4MP image in 2.6 seconds versus 12.4. Hydrogen 1.0 scores 38.33% on Frontier Science Research at $0.25 per problem, and Liquid AI's LFM3 1.7B fits in about 1 GB at 4-bit. The video is not sponsored.
items.author: Matthew Berman

items.title: AI News: New ChatGPT & Google Models (14 Updates Worth Knowing)
items.summary: Matt Wolfe's weekly roundup includes OpenAI Images 2.6 with GIF creation, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash making clips of up to 15 seconds at about $0.07 per second at 720p (three free videos a month in Google Vids), and Pika H3 Flex as a 220 GB open-weight release. Claude can now read bank data through Plaid for Pro, Max and Ultra plans, and Uber reported 500 AI-agent Uber Eats orders out of 320 million trips. Optimizely sponsors a segment (5:05 to 6:11).
items.author: Matt Wolfe

items.title: Ripple 65B: A Chip Design Lab Just Beat Every US Open Model
items.summary: Sam Witteveen tests Ripple 65B, a dense open-weight model from chip-design company Ricursive trained on 12 trillion tokens with a 1M-token context. Ricursive reports a Terminal Bench 2.1 score of 80.52, which it calls the best US open-weight result. Witteveen runs it locally with the DeepSeek harness. The video is not sponsored; the benchmark figures are the company's own.
items.author: Sam Witteveen

items.title: Weight space programming, science agents, 3D generators, new Gemini Omni, new GPT Image: AI NEWS
items.summary: AI Search packs about 35 research demos and releases into 48 minutes, with timestamps for each. The set includes weight-space programming (12:01), Hydrogen 1.0 for science (31:59), Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, GPT Images 2.6, 3D generators, Kimi K3.1 and Ripple 65B. Higgsfield sponsors a segment at 16:59.
items.author: AI Search

items.title: The Future of AI Is Absolutely Incredible (Spencer Huang)
items.summary: Two Minute Papers interviews NVIDIA's Spencer Huang on physical AI and simulation. Isaac Lab is moving from PhysX to the Newton physics framework, Sonic is a 42-million-parameter whole-body-control model, and conventional physics simulation is being paired with neural world simulators. Huang breaks the sim-to-real gap into data collection, generation, training, evaluation and deployment. Lambda sponsors the video near the end.
items.author: Two Minute Papers

sections.title: Tutorials Worth Watching
sections.description: Step-by-step builds for games, video and agent pipelines.

items.title: Claude Opus 5.5 is INCREDIBLE at building video games
items.summary: Alex Finn builds a third-person roguelike demon-slayer game in Unity with Opus 5.5, starting from a sword-combat vertical slice (chapters at 9:23 and 13:40) and then adding graphics (21:28) and assets (25:10). The 35-minute session shows the order of work from playable core to polish. His description promotes a free HubSpot playbook.
items.author: Alex Finn
key_takeaways: He starts with one playable combat loop before touching art.
Graphics and assets come in later passes once the game feels right.
Opus 5.5 is driving a real engine (Unity), not a toy web demo.
suggested_actions: Define a one-room vertical slice for your own game idea and have the agent build only that.
Hold asset and graphics requests until the core loop is playable.

items.title: The Future of Video Production is Here!
items.summary: Curious Refuge shows a pipeline that turns recorded audio plus a reference video into finished video: clean the voice in Adobe Podcast, build a black video, run it through Seedance 2.5, and compare against HeyGen and a MiniMax H3 LoRA. A costs chapter at 8:43 gives no figures.
items.author: Curious Refuge
key_takeaways: The chain is audio cleanup, reference video, then generation, so the voice recording drives the result.
Seedance 2.5 is compared directly with HeyGen and a MiniMax H3 LoRA.
The video skips actual cost numbers, so test pricing yourself.
suggested_actions: Record a 30-second voice clip, clean it in Adobe Podcast, and run it through the first two steps.
Run one clip through two of the generators and compare the lip sync.

items.title: My AI Software Factory Ships Hundreds of PRs a Week (Here's How I Manage It)
items.summary: Cole Medin shows an open-source mission-control dashboard built on Archon workflows and Neon Postgres that manages an AI software factory shipping hundreds of pull requests a week. He traced 21 failures back to workflow issues rather than model quality. Viktor sponsors a segment at 4:17 and Neon is also promoted.
items.author: Cole Medin
key_takeaways: The dashboard sits on Archon workflows and a Postgres store.
Of the failures he reviewed, 21 traced to workflow design, not the model.
The tool is open source, so the setup can be copied.
suggested_actions: Log every failed agent run for a week and label each as workflow or model.
Try the dashboard on a single repository before widening it.

sections.title: Use Cases to Borrow
sections.description: Founders, creators and scientists showing what works in real workflows.

items.title: How The #1 AI Engineer in The World Actually Uses AI
items.summary: In 5 minutes, Nick Saraev describes how Andrej Karpathy uses Claude Code: Opus 5.5 at medium effort, short plain-English prompts, and cheap filters first with Sonnet sub-agents after. He cites Karpathy's HackerTube project as the example. The workflow is Saraev's account, not Karpathy's own.
items.author: Nick Saraev
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: run a cheap filter over everything first and send only the survivors to a stronger model. It cuts cost on any large review job, such as support tickets or contracts.

items.title: AI Automation | Every AI Business Ranked from Worst to Best
items.summary: Nate Herk ranks 13 AI business models and argues that selling judgment is more durable than selling tools. He cites about 560K App Store apps in the first half of the year, a 187% rise in AI integration work on Upwork, workshops at $1,000 to $5,000, audits at $1,000 to $15,000 and chief AI officer pay of $280K to $650K. These are the video's figures.
items.author: Nate Herk
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: package an AI audit or workshop as a fixed-price offer. Herk's price bands give a ready benchmark for pricing your own advisory work.

items.title: Domu is AI that Negotiates
items.summary: YC Root Access profiles Domu, which uses AI agents to collect debt for buy-now-pay-later lenders. The founders say they collect $186 for every $100 a human team collects, that four of the five largest US BNPL companies are customers, and that they raised a $15M Series A. Calls are monitored with human feedback loops.
items.author: YC Root Access
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: pick one high-volume conversation that already has a clear success metric, such as dollars recovered, and let an agent run it with human review of the calls.

items.title: Building Physical AI for the Industrial World
items.summary: Tractian's CEO tells YC how the company grew to more than $100M in ARR (90% year over year) with sensors, software and AI that monitor 350,000 industrial assets. He describes visiting 88 factories in year one, using paid pilots with set success criteria, and moving from alerts toward autonomous operations. The figures are the company's.
items.author: YC Root Access
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: structure a pilot as a paid engagement with written success criteria and an agreed next step, so serious buyers separate from tire-kickers.

items.title: AI Is Now Doing Things Scientists Thought Were Impossible
items.summary: TheAIGRID reports that GPT-6 Astra scored 49 of 50 on the Theo Phys Eval after experts corrected errors in some reference solutions, and that AI review flagged serious errors in about a third of Frontier Math problems, most of which Epoch AI considered valid. It also covers a physicist who says AI solved a conjecture in two minutes after a year of his own work. Figures are as stated in the video.
items.author: TheAIGRID
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: use an AI reviewer to audit your own reference answers and benchmark sets before using them to grade vendors or internal models.

emerging_signals.pattern: Autonomous labs and science agents are moving from announcements to shown workflows.
emerging_signals.evidence: PNNL's autonomous materials lab (Nov 2), Nature papers on an AI-native autonomous lab (Nov 4) and agents that design a robot lab (Nov 6), TheAIGRID on AI finding errors in physics and math benchmarks (Nov 3), and Cambridge's Data2BEM agents, which cut building-energy-model creation from 8 hours for an expert to 48 minutes.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Whether more national labs and universities publish their own videos, and whether building-performance simulation groups (IBPSA-USA runs a webinar series on AI through January) show agent workflows.

emerging_signals.pattern: Solo builders are replacing paid apps with their own, and creators are publishing their agent setups within days.
emerging_signals.evidence: Berman on custom software and Artcraft (Nov 3), Riley Brown's focus monitor (Nov 2), Wolfe's Claude video editing (Nov 4), Alex Finn's Unity roguelike (Nov 4).
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Maintenance and distribution: which of these personal tools get shared as open-source projects.

emerging_signals.pattern: Open-weight releases now cover frontier-size, on-device and specialist models in the same week.
emerging_signals.evidence: Kimi K3.1 Pro, NorthCUA, Pika H3 Flex, Liquid AI LFM3 and Hydrogen 1.0 in Berman's and AI Search's roundups; Ripple 65B in Witteveen's test.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Independent replication of the self-reported benchmark scores.

emerging_signals.pattern: Weight-space programming gives models a new way to edit other models.
emerging_signals.evidence: MIT CSAIL's research post (Nov 2) covered by Two Minute Papers (Nov 7) and AI Search (12:01), and mentioned by Berman.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Whether the method works on models beyond Qwen3.5-0.8B; Gemma 3 270M showed no gain.
